note: Internet radio and podcast streaming, San Francisco. Stingray Group closed its purchase of TuneIn Holdings in December 2025 for up to $175M in cash (Stingray's release), so the row is acquired; the three sibling books still read private and are staler. Entry: TuneIn's funding ran $6M from Sequoia in 2010, $16M in August 2012 and $25M in May 2013 (Wikipedia and the Guardian, which puts the total at $47M since the first round in 2010, exactly those three); the Guardian names Google Ventures among the previous investors in the May 2013 round IVP led, and Wikipedia gives the 2010 round to Sequoia alone, so GV entered in the August 2012 round, the company's second institutional round (a Series B, Growth). No source names GV in that round in words, hence model at medium.

Peer-to-peer car rental marketplace (RelayRides until 2015), San Francisco (the S-1's principal office). Disputes the pre-filled status: 'defunct' came from a Wikidata join dated 1988, while Turo operates, filed S-1 amendments through November 2024 and withdrew its IPO in February 2025 (EDGAR). Mark: IAC's $250M Series E of July 2019 gave Turo 'a valuation of over $1 billion' (Yahoo Finance); the figure is that stated floor, no later priced round is on record, and the mark is older than 24 months, so stale. Disputes the Pre-Seed band: the band anchored on a 2009 filing (sold $672,500) that carries no GV person, before GV's 2010 vehicle existed. GV 2010, L.P. holds Turo stock (the S-1); TechCrunch (September 2011) names Google Ventures, August Capital and Shasta among the $10M raised to date, and (October 2011) calls that financing the Series A, which GM Ventures' $3M extension took to $13M; the Series A's first close is the Form D sold from 2010-12-14, the month CNET called the company 'Google-backed'. The Series B ($25M, Canaan) followed in June 2014 with Google Ventures named as a previous investor. Model at medium: no single page names GV in the Series A in words.

funding_rounds.round: Series A (first close; $13M in all with GM Ventures' extension)

note: Online marketplace for limited-edition contemporary art, Austin (the 2016 Form D address; David Krane is a director on it). Fate not established: the last dated news is the January 2018 CEO change (PR Newswire), and twyla.com shows only a 'pardon our dust' holding page. No source read gives a shutdown or a sale, so unknown, aligned with IVP's row. The pre-filled Series A band (the $19.3M 2016 round) stands.

Uber Technologies (NYSE: UBER), San Francisco. Disputes the pre-filled NL, a one-word Wikidata join to Uber's Dutch holding entity; the operating headquarters is San Francisco (EDGAR business address, 1725 3rd Street). Market cap $139.22B as of 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis.com), fresher than the siblings' September figures, same band. Entry: Google Ventures put $257.79M into Uber's August 2013 round, its largest deal then, at about $3.76B post-money (TechCrunch); the round's shares were Series C-1 and C-2 and existing investor Benchmark added $15M (TechCrunch), after the 2011 Series A and B the Benchmark and Menlo rows cite, so Growth.

Video coaching app for athletes (Cambridge, Mass. in 2012, Boston at the sale). Ubersense announced a $1.1M seed with Atlas Venture, Google Ventures and Boston Seed Capital in September 2012 (TechCrunch). Hudl acquired it in September 2014; the team stayed in Boston, and it had raised $2.5M in all from the same three investors (Re/code). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Online courses and nanodegrees, Mountain View. Accenture acquired it in May 2024 (Wikipedia; the firm's own exit line agrees). Entry: Google Ventures joined the $105M Series D of November 2015 as a new investor, in the Bertelsmann-led round that valued Udacity at $1B (TechCrunch); a16z, CRV and Drive were the existing investors. Growth.

Cloud contact-center software, San Francisco. GV led the $25M Series B of February 2018; the other participants were returning investors Kleiner Perkins and DCM and new backer Citi Ventures (TechCrunch), so GV was new at the B: Growth. Later rounds include a $76M Series D in September 2024 (Business Wire headline); no priced round at $1B or more is on record.

Generative AI for enterprise content, San Francisco ('a San Francisco-based generative AI startup', Crunchbase News; Lightspeed's row says Palo Alto). Entry: GV's first 'Invested' month is February 2023 (the firm's /ai list), when Typeface emerged from stealth with $65M from Lightspeed, GV, M12 and Menlo (TechCrunch, Crunchbase News); no page names that round, but the next one, $100M led by Salesforce Ventures in June 2023 with GV participating, is named Series B, and the Lightspeed and Menlo rows record their own firms' pages labelling the launch round Series A, so model at medium. Mark: the Series B valued Typeface at $1B (TechCrunch, 2023-06-29), exactly the band edge, older than 24 months, so stale. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on the name, twice): no later priced round and no acquisition; the company still ships product in September 2026; the only newer valuation line is a vendor estimate (GetLatka), which never bands.

AI echocardiography analysis for heart failure, Oxford (the Series C release is datelined Oxford, England). Entry: GV's first 'Invested' month on its /ai list is August 2021, the month Ultromics completed its $33M Series B (Cardiac Rhythm News headline; the article body is not readable to us), and the July 2025 $55M Series C release names GV among the continuing investors. No page names GV in the Series B in words, hence model at medium; Growth either way. No priced round at $1B or more is on record.

AI-plus-human translation platform with headquarters in Lisbon and San Francisco (Wikipedia). TransPerfect acquired it in August 2025 (TransPerfect's release; Wikipedia); the Portuguese entity left behind was declared insolvent in June 2026 (Portugal Resident), after the sale, so the row reads acquired. Entry: the $1.5M seed of May 2014 with Google Ventures among the investors (Wikipedia; TechCrunch names Kevin Rose of Google Ventures, July 2014). Graduation: a $5M Series A in October 2016 and a $23M Series B in January 2018 (TechCrunch). Country kept at the pre-filled US with San Francisco as the city; Headline's row reads Lisbon and PT and YC's San Francisco and US, so the two siblings already disagree and the dual headquarters is flagged for the A/B pass.

Universe (univer.se), the no-code website builder for iPhone, Brooklyn (TechCrunch; the Series B release is datelined Brooklyn), so New York. Disputes both pre-fills: the Wikidata join ('acquired by Arcs', dated 2017, and CZ) is a different entity; this company raised a $30M Series B led by Addition in December 2021, won a 2023 Apple Design Award, launched an AI designer in July 2023 (TechCrunch) and its site still sells, so private. The GC and YC sibling rows carry the same stale Wikidata status (acquired, defunct) and are flagged for alignment. Entry: GV's M.G. Siegler led the $10M Series A of April 2020 and took a board seat (TechCrunch); the company had raised $7.2M before from BoxGroup and General Catalyst. The December 2021 release names Google Ventures among the existing investors. No priced round at $1B or more is on record.

Upbound (upbound.io), the company behind the Crossplane cloud control plane, Seattle (its Form D address). Disputes the pre-filled public status and the $1.41B float: the weak CIK join picked up Upbound Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: UPBD, the former Rent-A-Center), a different company. This Upbound is private and still ships product (August 2026 platform launch). The pre-filled Series A band (the $9M 2018 round, Dave Munichiello a director) stands; the later $52M round of November 2021 carries no disclosed valuation, and no priced round at $1B or more is on record.

AI lending marketplace (NASDAQ: UPST). Its latest 10-Q (filed 2026-08-04) gives the principal executive office as 220 Park Road, Burlingame; the First Round and Khosla rows still read San Mateo and are staler. Entry: the $1.75M seed that came with the April 2012 launch, from First Round, Kleiner Perkins, NEA, Google Ventures, Crunchfund and Mark Cuban (Wikipedia). Graduation: the $5.9M Series A that followed (Wikipedia), a named later round, so graduated whatever the amounts.

Consumer cloud storage built by Apple and Oracle veterans, Palo Alto (TechCrunch, 2015). Western Digital acquired it in August 2017 (TechCrunch). Stage undetermined: Upthere never disclosed the size or number of its rounds (TechCrunch, 2015); it came out of beta in July 2016 with $77M raised in all from KPCB and Western Digital (leads) with Floodgate, Elevation Partners, GV, NTT Docomo Ventures and Square 1 Bank, and no page ties GV to a named round. The firm has listed it since 2013 (the year is an anchor from the archive, not an entry label).

Urban mobility and location analytics, Los Altos (aligned with a16z's row). Google acquired it in September 2016 (Wikipedia; the firm's own exit line). Stage undetermined: at its May 2014 launch Urban Engines had raised an undisclosed amount from Google Ventures, Eric Schmidt, Ram Shriram, a16z and SV Angel (TechCrunch), and Wikipedia says the round was led by Google Ventures, but no source names it.

Robotics and AI that reclaim lumber from construction and demolition waste, Oakland (the seed release is datelined Oakland, CA). Lowercarbon Capital and GV led the $5.6M seed, announced 9 December 2022, with Union Labs and Catapult Ventures following on (the company's release). A 2025 raise appears only on a data-vendor page, which cannot cite a round. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Wes McKinney's Apache Arrow company. Its own announcement (10 December 2020) says it raised $4.9M in seed funding led by GV with Walden International, Nepenthe, Amplify Partners and RStudio; GV's /ai list dates the investment October 2020. Ursa folded into Voltron Data in 2021 (Ursa Labs' site now reads 'Ursa Labs is now Voltron Data Labs', and Voltron Data was launched by staff from Nvidia, Ursa Computing and BlazingSQL, TechCrunch), so acquired by merger. No source read places Ursa Computing in a city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Mobile deep-linking product ads, San Francisco (YC Summer 2012). Pinterest acquired it in 2016 (the firm's own exit line). Entry: the $3.1M seed of October 2013 lists Google Ventures among the investors (TechCrunch). Graduation: Accel led a $12M round in April 2014 at a $40M valuation with Google Ventures following (TechCrunch); the round is unnamed, and $12M clears max(2 x $3.1M, $5M).

Oxford vaccine and T-cell immunotherapy spin-out (renamed Barinthus Biotherapeutics in 2023). Disputes the pre-filled public status: Clywedog's holding company acquired all of Barinthus's shares under a scheme of arrangement effective 9 September 2026, making it a wholly owned subsidiary (the 8-K), and the ADSs were delisted; the firm's exit line 'NASDAQ: VACC' is stale (decisions D8). Entry: entities affiliated with GV (GV Europe 2014 and GV 2017) bought 5,516 Series A shares for GBP 6.0M in the Series A that opened in November 2017 (the S-1's related-party table); the firm's own post dates GV's investment to 2017. Country: GB confirmed at entry (the S-1 gives Oxford); the principal executive office moved from Harwell, Oxfordshire to Germantown, Maryland by the FY2025 10-K, so the last-known city is Germantown and the pair is flagged city_country_conflict for Erik.

FP&A and strategic finance planning software. GV led the $20M Series A in 2021 after Menlo Ventures led the $4.2M seed in the summer of 2020 (TechCrunch, 2021-10-01), so GV entered at the A. City: TechCrunch calls it 'Mountain View-based'; Menlo's row reads San Francisco without a citation, so the two books disagree and the city is flagged for the A/B pass. Status: operating and independent (its own site, footer 2025; product releases through April 2024). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News on the name): no priced round at $1B or more; the newest items are 2022-2024 product and hiring releases.

Cross-border B2B payments (Align Commerce until March 2017), San Francisco (Wikipedia). Entry: GV was a new investor in the $24M round led by NAB Ventures that came with the rebrand in March 2017, which took total funding past $40M (TechCrunch); the company had already raised more than $16M in earlier rounds, so the $24M round was its Series B or later. No page names the round, hence model at medium; Growth either way. A $31M raise followed in 2020 (Business Insider headline); no priced round at $1B or more is on record.

Structural-immunology drug discovery (NLRP3 and innate immunity), Waltham, Mass. with research in Montreal (the launch release's dateline). Disputes the Growth band: the band read the $60M 2020 filing against the era's Series A ceiling, but the company names it: 'a $60 million Series A financing led by founding investor Versant Ventures with participation by GV' (6 May 2020), with GV's Brendan Bulik-Sullivan quoted and a director on the filing, so Series A. The pre-filled entry date (2019-11-18, that Series A's first sale) stands. Later rounds: $100M Series B (April 2021), $140M Series C led by SoftBank (February 2022), then a Novo Nordisk licensing deal; no sale and no priced round at $1B or more is on record.

3D sensing and safety software for industrial robots, Waltham. Symbotic bought it for $8.7M in August 2024, taking most of its IP and staff (The Robot Report); the firm's exit line agrees. Entry: GV's $12M Series A in 2017, with Lux Capital joining and GV's Andy Wheeler taking a board seat, after a $1M seed from Siemens' venture arm (The Robot Report); GV's /ai list dates its first investment September 2017 (the entry date, D7). A $29M Series B followed in 2023 (TechCrunch).

Immunology biotech (atacicept), NASDAQ: VERA; renamed from Trucode Gene Repair in April 2020 and from CDF Therapeutics before that (the S-1). Current principal office 2000 Sierra Point Parkway, Brisbane (EDGAR). Entry: the S-1's beneficial-ownership table shows GV 2017, L.P. holding only Series B preferred and GV 2019, L.P. the Series C; Kleiner Perkins held the Series A and B. Trucode emerged from stealth in September 2019 with $34M from Kleiner Perkins and GV (Fierce Biotech, BioSpace), which dates the Series B GV bought. Growth. The base also carries this company as 'trucode' (the firm listed TruCode in 2019-2021): one company, two rows.

funding_rounds.round: Series B (announced with $34M in total financing)

note: Real-world clinical data from specialty-society registries, San Francisco. GV led the $30M Series C of July 2018, with Biomatics Capital, GE Ventures, Lagunita Biosciences and Brook Byers named as the existing investors (MedCity News), so GV entered at the C: Growth. By February 2020 the company had raised $100M from GV, Bain Capital Ventures, Casdin and Define (TechCrunch), and GV joined the $150M Series E of January 2022 as an existing investor (Verana's release). No priced round at $1B or more is on record.

Frontend cloud and the Next.js framework, San Francisco. Entry: GV's /ai list dates its first investment December 2020, and the firm's own post of 16 December 2020 says Vercel had 'just announced its Series B funding, led by GV', so the Series B was GV's entry: Growth. The pre-filled $9.3B (the September 2025 Series F) stands.

Grid connection and power dispatch software for data centers and large energy buyers (verse.inc), San Francisco. Disputes the Seed band: both Form Ds were filed together in 2024 with the same directors, so the band's 2022 anchor is the seed Coatue led, not GV's. Verse's own release (22 May 2024): 'our $20.5M Series A funding round led by Google Ventures, with notable participation from our lead seed round investor, Coatue', so GV entered at the Series A. Bessemer led the $54M Series B in June 2026 with GV participating (GlobeNewswire); no valuation was disclosed. Coatue's book carries the same company as 'verse' (private, below $1B, San Francisco), and this row agrees.

PCSK9 gene-editing medicines; acquired by Eli Lilly in 2025 (the pre-filled status; the firm's exit line 'NASDAQ: VERV' is stale). Last principal office 201 Brookline Avenue, Boston (EDGAR). Disputes the Growth band, which read the January 2021 Series B filing: the S-1's related-party tables show GV 2017, L.P. buying $7.0M of the Series A in its first closing of August 2018 (then further tranches in 2019 and 2020), and the firm's own post says 'GV led the $58.5M Series A'. GV 2019 then bought Series A-2 (2020) and $5M of the $94M Series B (2021).

Identity and authorization security, Palo Alto (aligned with the sibling rows). ServiceNow announced the purchase in December 2025 and completed it on 2 March 2026 (CRN Asia), so acquired, aligned with BCV's row (Accel's still reads private and is staler). Entry: the firm's own post says 'When GV led Veza's Series B in 2021', and its April 2022 post calls GV 'an early investor'; no firm page shows an earlier GV round, so the Series B is read as the entry: Growth, medium because the post does not say 'first' in words.

Protein stabilization (DUBTAC) spun out of Novartis and UC Berkeley, South San Francisco (Crunchbase News). It launched in July 2022 with a $65M Series A co-led by a16z and Deerfield, with Droia, GV, The Mark Foundation and the Berkeley Catalyst Fund participating (a16z's announcement), the company's first financing, so GV entered at the A. No later priced round is on record.

Marketplace turning artists' designs into apparel and accessories (YC Summer 2017), San Francisco. Cimpress acquired it in 2018 (the firm's own exit line; YC's row agrees). Entry: the $1.3M seed disclosed in November 2014, with Google Ventures' M.G. Siegler and Dave Munichiello named as its investors in VIDA (TechCrunch). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Outbound-link monetization for publishers, San Francisco; merged into Sovrn in 2018 (the firm's exit line; now Sovrn Commerce), so acquired. Disputes the Pre-Seed band: the record names the $800,000 round of 2009 'seed funding from First Round Capital and Google Ventures' (Wikipedia; the Form D of June 2009 sold exactly $800,000), so Seed; the pre-filled entry date stands. Graduation: a $5.4M Series B led by Emergence Capital in March 2011 with Google Ventures and First Round following (Wikipedia), a named later round. First Round's row still carries the Pre-Seed band on the same round.

Infectious-disease immunology biotech (NASDAQ: VIR), San Francisco (EDGAR business address). Entry: GV 2017, L.P. signed Vir's Amended and Restated Investors' Rights Agreement dated 29 November 2017 as an investor (the S-1 exhibit); the S-1 shows only Series A-1 and A-2 preferred outstanding then, with the Series B issued in January 2019, so GV's position was bought in the Series A-1 financing of 2016-2018. Series A, medium because the exhibit does not state the series GV bought.

funding_rounds.round: Series A-1 (GV an investor-rights party by this date)

note: Extra-uterine support (EXTEND) for extremely premature infants, out of CHOP, Philadelphia (its own site gives 2301 Chestnut Street). Sands Capital led the $50M Series B of November 2024 'with participation from Google Ventures (GV), First Spark Ventures, Flerie and Khosla Ventures', and GV's Cathy Friedman is a board observer (the company's release). The only earlier financing on record is an unlabeled $25M round of August 2022 whose investors we could not read, and the firm first lists Vitara in 2024; the Series B is read as GV's entry, model at medium because no page says GV was new. Growth.

AI stroke detection and care coordination, San Francisco (with Tel Aviv R&D). Entry: GV's /ai list dates its first investment June 2018; Kleiner Perkins led the $21M round announced in July 2018 'with participation from Google's GV fund' after Innovation Endeavors' $7.5M round (Globes), and the next round, $50M in October 2019, is named Series B with GV and Kleiner as existing investors (NoCamels), so the $21M round was the Series A; no page names it, hence model at medium. Mark: the $100M Series D of April 2022 at $1.2B, co-led by Tiger Global and Insight with GV following (Insight's release), older than 24 months, so stale; aligned with Insight's row.

Open-source voice AI framework for developers (YC Winter 2023), San Francisco (Business Insider). Entry: the $3.25M seed from Y Combinator, Base10, GV, Gradient, Accel and Liquid2, closed in the weeks after YC's demo day (Business Insider, February 2024); GV's /ai list dates the investment April 2023. Status aligned with YC's row, whose directory lists Vocode as acquired; no source read names an acquirer, and vocode.dev now redirects to the company's GitHub organization, last active November 2024. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News twice, one web search): no priced round at $1B or more. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

AI meeting assistant (Voicera, legal name Rizio, Inc.); Cisco acquired it in 2019 (the firm's exit line; Headline's row agrees). Entry: the $13.5M Series A of March 2018 led by e.ventures, with GV among the enterprise investors (TechCrunch); GV's /ai list dates the investment March 2018. City: Rizio's Form Ds of December 2017 and March 2018 give Menlo Park (earlier ones Los Altos); Headline's row reads San Jose without a source, so the books disagree and the city is flagged for the A/B pass.

Bitcoin and Lightning payment infrastructure (voltage.cloud). Disputes the pre-filled JP, a one-word Wikidata join to a Japanese namesake: the seed release is datelined Wichita, Kansas. Entry: the $6M seed of January 2022 led by Trammell Venture Partners with Craft Ventures, GV and others (the company's release). Status: operating (a Lightning credit line launched February 2026). Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News): no priced round at $1B or more; the '$2.5 billion' Voltage Park headline is a different company. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

GPU-accelerated Apache Arrow analytics (Theseus), Mountain View (aligned with Battery and Coatue). Shut down: it announced its closure in late 2025 (Andy Pavlo's 2025 databases retrospective, CMU), after halving its staff in 2024; defunct, aligned with Coatue's row (Battery and Lightspeed still read private and are staler). Entry: GV was in the $22M seed led by BlackRock and Walden and in the $88M Series A led by Walden Catalyst, announced together in February 2022 (TechCrunch); GV also held Ursa Computing, whose team co-founded Voltron. Graduation: the named Series A.

In-app video advertising (AngelPad), San Francisco. Blackstone acquired it in July 2019 for a reported $750M or more (TechCrunch). Entry: the $2M seed of May 2012 includes Google Ventures (TechCrunch). Graduation: the $6.5M Series A led by Crosslink in August 2013 with Google Ventures participating (TechCrunch); a $17M Series B followed in 2014.

Health and beauty products for people of color (Bevel). Procter & Gamble acquired it in December 2018 and the team moved to Atlanta (TechCrunch), the last-known city. Entry: Google Ventures is named in the $24M Series B of September 2015 led by IVP (TechCrunch); the $2.4M seed and the a16z-led $6.9M Series A of June 2014 list no Google Ventures (TechCrunch), so GV entered at the B: Growth.

AI-driven prescription drug marketplaces, Chicago. EVERSANA acquired it on 26 August 2025, with Waltz's CEO Mark Thierer becoming EVERSANA's CEO (pharmaphorum, EVERSANA's own news site); the firm's exit line agrees. Stage from the company's own Form D sequence (CIK 1880783, filing first as Asset Blue Pharmacy Services, Inc.): a $3M equity round of August 2021 with only the founders as related persons, then the $35M offering first sold 2022-01-14 with GV's Benjamin Robbins a director, filed from Google's Cambridge office; one earlier filing and $35M under the 2022 Series A ceiling ($40M) give Series A. It launched publicly with the $35M in April 2022. Replaces the pre-filled entry date (2024-11-26, the later $20M filing); GV's 2022 post already lists Waltz among Ben Robbins's investments.

Wander, the social diary app Days (TechStars NY 2012), New York. Yahoo acquired it in February 2014 for a reported price above $10M and the team joined Yahoo's New York mobile group (TechCrunch). Entry: the $1.2M seed of April 2012 from SV Angel, Google Ventures and others (the Observer); it was all Wander ever raised (TechCrunch). Redpoint's 'wander' row is a different company (the vacation-home network founded 2021): a name collision, not aligned. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Warp (warp.dev), the Rust terminal turned agentic development environment, New York (the 2020 Form D of Denver Technologies, Inc., Warp's legal name, gives 11 Prince Street, New York, with Erik Nordlander a director). Entry: GV led the $6M seed (TechCrunch; the firm's own post: 'Shortly thereafter, GV led Warp's seed financing'), first sold 2020-06-02 on that Form D. Graduation: the $17M Series A led by Dylan Field, announced April 2022 (TechCrunch). Sequoia led a $50M Series B in June 2023. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News twice): no priced round at $1B or more. Battery's and YC's 'warp' rows are a different company (the payroll startup): a name collision, not aligned.

Microdrama streaming app with a fan social network (watchclubtv.com; legal name Kino Technologies Inc.), founded by a former Meta product manager. 'The idea alone was interesting enough to secure seed funding led by GV' (TechCrunch, 3 February 2026). No source read places the company in a city; US from its Inc. legal name. The entry is inside the 24-month window, so censored.
